claims.statement: In the three added metadata-reference scenarios, the `VerifyCS.Test` phase expects zero diagnostics and passes at head: keyed generic struct, the issue's keyed generic record struct, and generic struct with an unkeyed property. Its actual scope is the single usage source plus an emitted metadata reference; `tests-without-change` confirms that this phase produces AD0001 and CS8785 with base source. `SkipGeneratedSourcesCheck` means this phase does not compare generated source text, and these results do not establish a command-line two-project build, the .NET 10 SDK, or other type shapes.

The separate direct `MessagePackGenerator` run in each added scenario has no generator-driver diagnostic whose severity is Warning or higher. The assertion is specifically `Assert.Empty` over `runResult.Diagnostics`; it does not assert analyzer diagnostics, lower-severity driver diagnostics, compiler diagnostics from a compilation updated with the generated trees, or runtime behavior.

Each direct generator run emits the expected resolver hint name: `TempProject.MyResolver.g.cs` for the two struct scenarios and `App.AppResolver.g.cs` for the record-struct scenario. `Assert.Contains` examines only generated hint names; it does not establish the resolver body, formatter registrations for the closed generic type, successful compilation of generated output, runtime serialization, or trimmed/NativeAOT usability.

claims.statement: Analyzer diagnostics routed through the modified `reportDiagnostic` callback are forwarded only when their location is in source and its syntax tree belongs to the collector's compilation; Location.None, metadata locations, and other-compilation source trees are dropped. The unkeyed-member test establishes the drop behavior for the consuming compilation's former metadata-member MsgPack004 diagnostic, whose base failure output is recorded, but it does not establish that the defining compilation reports that problem or exhaustively test the forwarding direction for every diagnostic.

claims.statement: The property `BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull` path no longer indexes `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]`; its helper returns the identifier location only when the first declaration syntax is a `PropertyDeclarationSyntax`, and otherwise returns null. None of the added tests uses a null key, so they do not directly execute this diagnostic branch. The pre-existing `MsgPack00xAnalyzerTests.NullStringKey` passes at both revisions, but its source and assertions are unavailable, so its exact declaration shape and what it establishes about metadata or positional-record properties cannot be determined.

claims.statement: The field `MemberNeedsKey` creation path now uses `FirstOrDefault()?.GetSyntax().GetLocation()`, so a field with no declaring syntax supplies a null location rather than being indexed at element zero in that expression. No listed test directly asserts this field path: the added unkeyed metadata member is a property, and no added field-based metadata case or field-specific diagnostic assertion is provided.

decisions.statement: The change chooses a consumer-side ownership policy for diagnostics concerning metadata members: suppress every diagnostic lacking a source tree in the current compilation, and document that the defining project reports such member problems.
decisions.whyHuman: The requirement specifies a clean valid repro and a generated resolver, but does not specify where diagnostics for invalid members of an already-built reference should appear, whether consuming-member fallback locations are desirable, or whether locationless diagnostics unrelated to metadata should also be dropped. Tests can observe the selected policy but cannot settle that user-facing tradeoff or whether the defining project will actually be analyzed.
options: Implemented: drop all diagnostics whose location is not a source tree in the current compilation, and state in README.md and MsgPack004.md that member problems belong to the defining project.
Report metadata-member diagnostics at the consuming member or another available source location in the using project.
Retain metadata or Location.None diagnostics where the analyzer driver permits them, while changing only the syntax accesses that throw.
Suppress only diagnostics known to concern metadata members, while continuing to forward unrelated locationless diagnostics.
Qualify the documentation to say that defining-project reporting depends on that project being built with the analyzer, without guaranteeing that every problem is reported elsewhere.

citations.quote:
Closed generic types defined in a referenced assembly (for example, `Item<int>` where `Item<T>` is defined in another project or NuGet package) can be used as members of your `[MessagePackObject]` types, including generic value types and record structs.
Diagnostics about the members of such a type are reported by the assembly that defines it rather than by the consuming project, so any problem must be fixed there.

This analyzer only reports on members declared in the project being compiled.
Members of a type defined in a referenced assembly are reported by the project that defines that type, so an unattributed public member of such a type must be fixed in its defining project.

decisions.statement: Regression coverage uses in-memory compilations with .NET 8 reference assemblies, defaulting to C# 7.3 except for the record-struct case, and checks a resolver hint name rather than running the attached two-project .NET 10 build or validating the complete resolver body.
decisions.whyHuman: The requirement does not prescribe the regression-test architecture. Executed tests can establish that this harness discriminates base from head, but cannot by themselves settle how much environment fidelity and generated-output validation is sufficient for the reported SDK, real project-reference, deployment, and runtime scenarios.
options: Implemented: compile the defining source to a metadata image, run the testing verifier and a separate generator driver, and assert diagnostics plus the resolver hint name.
Add an integration regression that builds the two actual projects with the reported SDK and inspects the consuming assembly.
Retain the in-memory reproduction but also compile generated output and assert resolver/formatter contents.
Use a combination of the in-memory tests and integration/runtime coverage for trimmed or NativeAOT consumption.

findings.statement: A source positional-record property can fall through the new `GetPropertyIdentifierLocation` helper because it recognizes only `PropertyDeclarationSyntax`, while the adjacent missing-key logic explicitly recognizes `ParameterSyntax` as well. For a positional property reaching `BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull` with both key forms null, the helper can therefore produce Location.None, after which the new report wrapper drops the diagnostic even though the declaration is in the current source compilation. The added tests use keyed properties and do not cover this null-key positional-record path; whether the pre-existing NullStringKey test covers it cannot be determined because its source is not supplied.

findings.statement: The documentation presents defining-project reporting as a guarantee, but the implementation only suppresses the diagnostic in the consuming compilation and the new helper emits the defining assembly without running analyzers on it. Consequently the tests do not establish that an unkeyed metadata member is reported anywhere; for an already-built project or NuGet reference, its defining project need not participate in the consuming build at all. The documentation would be inaccurate for such a case even though consumer-side suppression itself is intentional.
